verdicts.note: Incumbent since January 2023 running on his first-term record [S1][S6], elected in 2022 [S7]. -1 rather than -2 is right because he came from outside law enforcement and graduated from the academy only in December 2023 [S6].

Attacked on single source: all of it is one forum report [S5]. It holds at -2 medium because the statement is explicit and general ('without raising taxes — of which I am opposed') and backed by a specific refusal to support a 0.1% sales tax increase, even while he says the office needs more deputies [S5]. Medium already reflects the single source. Minor basis wording: the dossier does not say the proposed sales tax was 'for public safety'; it says only that he was asked to support it [S5].

Rebuilt detective and internal affairs units, solved cases, 'the sheriff's office is the drug task force' and a marine unit [S3][S4] on the enforcement side; help from trained mental health professionals 'whenever possible' and a co-responding crisis responder [S3] on the prevention side. -1 fits the mix.
Says more deputies are needed (pole b) but will manage with existing staff and opposes a tax increase to pay for them (pole a) [S5]. Genuinely mixed; 0 medium is right.

The +1 treats Byrd as the 'new voice' because he is the challenger and has not held elected office [S1]. In this race that misreads the axis. Byrd spent about 20 years in this same office, rising to lieutenant, and runs on that career [S1][S4]; the contest overview and the incumbent's dossier show that Garcia is the one who came from outside law enforcement. Byrd has named a former police chief as undersheriff [S3][S6] and left the office in 2010-2011 when then-Sheriff Didion lost [S3][S6], so he represents the office's former leadership returning, not outsider energy. Against that, he has been out of policing for about 15 years and is challenging an incumbent. The two pull in opposite directions; 0 represents it better than +1.

Restraint is his main budget message: the budget 'has doubled', calls for more money are 'ludicrous', 'we have to do better with what we have', and administrators' overtime and flex time should be cut [S6][S4][S5]. But -2 means fully pole a, and the dossier records expansion planks too: restore the drug task force 'day one' [S5], rebuild a dedicated drug enforcement effort [S4], and expand designated crisis responders and co-responder programs toward seven-day coverage using state grants [S4]. Grant-funded program expansion is pole b even when it avoids new county money. -1 fits.

Dedicated drug enforcement to arrest traffickers and the task force 'day one' [S4][S5] on the enforcement side; treatment access, expanded crisis responders and co-responders, and community-oriented policing [S4][S5] on the prevention side. Enforcement leads, so -1.
